topic: Which trade-offs between lens compactness and gain roll-off are critical for maintaining reliable downlink during satellite orbital motion?
consensus_response: The critical trade-offs between lens compactness and gain roll-off for reliable downlink during satellite orbital motion arise from the physical mechanisms of array factor, interference, and spreading effects. Compact lenses amplify interference from adjacent beams, increasing atmospheric scattering in LEO orbits. Smaller lens sizes increase atmospheric interference, reducing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Gain roll-off affects the beam's width, increasing spreading effects and reducing SNR. These trade-offs impact the 'budget' of the design in terms of performance, capacity, and interference.
reference_context: Optical data links may not always outperform RF data links for downlink applications from LEO satellites. However, whenever onboard sensors have very large acquisition rates, and a reasonable buffer size is available, optical links may indeed offer better system performance than RF solutions.
